subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & qualification — LumenHealth
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Oct 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist & qualification — LumenHealth

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and appreciate the clarity on the three priority flows you highlighted (clinical summarization, triage routing, and patient Q&A). Per our demo, I wanted to capture a concise recommended shortlist, the tradeoffs we observed, and the asks we need to run a focused eval to validate fit for your SLA and hallucination tolerance.

Recommended model shortlist (post-demo, prioritized by fit -> cost):
- rw-infer-13b-int8 (primary): best balance for clinical summarization quality vs cost; quantized evals show ~18% cost reduction vs full fp16 with ~3–5% quality delta on medical QA tasks. Latency (single-request median, 512 tokens): ~120–160ms on our Dedicated XPU pool.
- llama3-medium-specialized (fallback): strong instruction-following on short answers (patient Q&A), lower throughput for long seqs; lower infra footprint but higher p95.
- opt-7b-hf-int4 (cheap burst): good for lightweight routing/triage classification at very low token cost; lower QA fidelity, recommended only for non-critical lookups.

Tradeoffs/notes:
- Cost: rw-infer-13b-int8 is the most cost-effective for sustained summarization loads thanks to prefix caching and continuous batching.
- Latency: if your p95 < 400ms requirement holds across 50 concurrent users, we recommend the Dedicated tier with autoscale cap set + burst capacity.
- Quality/regression: we saw some targeted hallucination patterns in the demo prompts for medication names (edge cases). We recommend running a 200-sample prompt regression set (we'll provide) before any rollout to monitor changes across versions.

Asks / next steps for a tightly scoped eval (target: 2-week sprint):
1) Confirm target SLOs (median and p95), expected concurrency, and peak requests/day.
2) Share a representative dataset (redacted) or allow us to run our sample prompt pack against a 200-case subset.
3) Allow a short Dedicated evaluation window (2–3 days) for rw-infer-13b-int8 so we can collect p50/p95 and error patterns with your real prompts.
4) Procurement: procurement contact and any specific compliance docs you need (SOC2 attachments, DPA).

I've attached a starter prompt pack and our lightweight benchmark CSV for the models above; Marissa is cc'd with the deeper perf artifacts and regression playbook. Happy to schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week once you confirm the eval window.

Best,
Rishi

Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifying questions before we schedule the eval:

1) The latency numbers you quoted (120–160ms) — are those median or p95? Can you share the p95 numbers for the 512-token summary case at ~50 concurrent users? Our clinical UX team is strict about p95.
2) For rw-infer-13b-int8, what guardrails do you recommend for the medication hallucination issue you mentioned? We need a remediation plan that doesn't materially increase latency.
3) On procurement: we can share our standard DPA and will loop in procurement if the price estimate looks within range. Can you send a ballpark monthly cost for the eval window + a 1-month pilot at expected throughput of ~200k tokens/day?

If you can get this in the next 24–48h, we'll aim to run the eval the week after next.

— Sara Klein
Head of Product, Clinical AI | LumenHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@lumenhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 09:12:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist & qualification — LumenHealth

Hi Sara / Rishi — jumping in with the technical attachments and quick answers to Sara's asks.

1) Latency at 50 concurrent users (512-token summary):
- rw-infer-13b-int8: p50 ~140ms, p95 ~420ms on Dedicated XPU pool with default batching (continuous batching enabled).
- llama3-medium-specialized: p50 ~95ms, p95 ~610ms (higher variance for long sequences).
- opt-7b-hf-int4: p50 ~60ms, p95 ~220ms (but lower QA fidelity).

2) Guardrail recommendations for medication hallucinations (minimal latency impact):
- Prefix-constrained generation + KG-check: run a lightweight post-generation validator that checks entity mentions against your canonical medication list (fast lookup, <10ms per request if cached).
- Prompt engineering: add constraint token that increases precision on medication spans (we'll share variants in the prompt pack).
- Thresholding + fallback: if validator confidence low, route to llama3-medium-specialized with a higher-beam/verification prompt (adds 50–120ms but used rarely).

3) Cost ballpark for requested windows (approx):
- 3-day Dedicated eval (rw-infer-13b-int8): ~$1,250 (includes reserved xPU time + token usage).
- 1-month pilot (200k tokens/day average): ~$6,500 — includes autoscale headroom and monitoring retention at 30 days.

Attachments & links included:
- benchmarks_q3_2028.csv (summary of p50/p95, token cost estimates, and regression delta for our medical QA prompt set).
- Lumen_demo_prompt_pack_v1.zip (your prompt samples + our curated regression set ~200 cases).
- Lumen_price_estimate_2028.pdf (ballpark numbers and line items).

Quick notes on regression monitoring: we'll run versioned prompt checks and generate a "quality delta" report after the eval; if any model shows >5% drop on F1/precision for medication entities vs baseline, we'll execute an automated rollback to the previous verified model.

Related links:
- Lightweight perf dashboard (read-only): https://redwood-internal.storage/benchmarks/lumen_demo_q3_2028
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8421

I'll seed the Drive folder with the prompt variants and a small script to run local validation checks. Let me know if you need the SOC2 artifact set early — procurement, I can share the SOC2 report link once you confirm the DPA.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
